answer: To resist sybils, require each new agent to lock a single unsplittable walnut bond and to be grafted onto an existing work vine that grows only when older, uncorrelated peers attest real tasks over time. Overnight clones behave like a willow that roots from every cut twig: they can multiply cheaply, but they share funders and timing, so the graph treats them as one unproven clump. Until their bond has aged and their attestations come from distinct histories, they carry no voting weight.
